Need the detailed dermatological examination record and clinical photographs documenting nail dystrophy, palmoplantar keratoderma, and oral leukokeratosis, as these phenotypic features are core clinical evidence to corroborate the de novo KRT6A mutation and confirm pachyonychia congenita while excluding mimics.

bindings.label: 9-year-old girl has thickened nails and keratinized plaques on palms, soles, and corners of mouth since birth
At age 1, fingernails and toenails began to turn yellow and thicken; skin of stressed parts of palms and soles gradually became keratinized, thickened, black and chapped.
No family history of similar symptoms.

Nail examination: fingernails and toenails partly thickened and raised in wedge shape, surface rough, opaque, and dirty brown; skin examination: dry skin on trunk and extremities, punctate and flaky keratinized dark brown thickened patches on palms and soles; oral examination: fissured tongue, oral leukokeratosis, and keratotic plaques in corners of mouth.
Physical examination showed normal vision, hearing, intelligence, and growth with moderate nutrition; no natal teeth, follicular sebaceous cysts, hair loss, or other organ abnormalities.
Genetic testing identifies heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del variant
Parental genetic testing is negative for the KRT6A variant in both parents, indicating a de novo mutation
Patient has Pachyonychia congenita caused by a de novo KRT6A mutation
Whole-exome sequencing and Sanger validation confirm the heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del variant
Skin biopsy and imaging were not obtained; molecular evidence was deemed sufficient for diagnosis
